name: Vector

name: East Ridge
beta: From the parking area, follow the remains of an old jeep track and then a worn climbers' path up grassy slopes to a saddle on the ridge at about 9,300-9,400 ft. Climb steeply up the ridge to around 10,200 ft, where it bends northwest, and continue up to about 10,800 ft. From here the ridge narrows and the scrambling becomes sustained: a series of short rock steps, roughly 10-30 ft high, around 11,000 ft form the crux, followed by long stretches of easier Class 2-3 scrambling to the summit. Stay on or very close to the crest, dropping just left of it when needed; the faces on either side quickly turn into Class 4-5 terrain.
overview: The East Ridge is the standard way up Diamond Peak, the highest summit in the Lemhi Range and one of Idaho's few ultra-prominent peaks. From a high trailhead reached by a rough dirt road, a short, steep climbers' path leads onto a long ridge that rises about 3,000 ft from treeline to the top. The upper half is a sustained Class 3 scramble with big views over the Birch Creek Valley far below.

current.approach: From Idaho Highway 28 in the Birch Creek Valley on the east side of the Lemhi Range, turn west on the signed Pass Creek Road (north of the old Blue Dome site). Beyond the first couple of miles the road fords Pass Creek and becomes rough; stay on the main track through a gate and into the national forest. The road finishes as rough jeep tracks to a small saddle with a fire ring at about 8,000 ft, where parties park.
current.descent: Descend the same way along the East Ridge, staying on the crest through the Class 3 steps, then follow the climbers' path back down the grassy slopes to the parking area.
current.detailed_rack: Winter: ice axe, snow anchors, ropes, harnesses; slipping with no axe to arrest could be fatal. Summer: easy scrambling with a handful of class 4 moves, maybe low class 5; a rope and prusik may calm novices. Short-rappel gear eases the descent.
